49 	Recent pronouncements :
(a) 	Newly applicable standards:
	
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has notified Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Amendment 
Rules, 2024 dated August 12, 2024, to introduce Ind AS 117 “Insurance Contracts”, replacing the existing Ind 
AS 104 “Insurance Contracts” and Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Second Amendment Rules, 
2024 dated September 09, 2024, to amend Ind AS 116.
	
These amendments are effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after April 01, 2024. The 
Company has applied these amendments for the first-time.
	
(i) 	 Introduction of Ind AS 117: Insurance Contracts
	
	
Ind AS 117 Insurance Contracts is a comprehensive new accounting standard for insurance contracts 
covering recognition and measurement, presentation and disclosure. Ind AS 117 applies to all types of 
insurance contracts, regardless of the type of entities that issue them as well as to certain guarantees 
and financial instruments with discretionary participation features.
	
	
The amendment has no impact on the Company’s financial statements.
	
(ii) 	 Lease Liability in a Sale and Leaseback - Amendments to Ind AS 116
	
	
The amendment specifies the requirements that a seller-lessee uses in measuring the lease liability 
arising in a sale and leaseback transaction to ensure the seller-lessee does not recognize any amount 
of the gain or loss that relates to the right of use asset it retains. 
	
	
The amendment is effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after April 01, 2024 and must 
be applied retrospectively to sale and leaseback transactions entered into after the date of initial 
application of Ind AS 116. 
	
	
The amendment has no impact on the Company’s financial statements.
(b)	 Standards issued/notified but not yet effective:
	
There are no standards that are notified and not yet effective as on the date.

Re-evaluation of EV and Net Zero goals
Our focused efforts on driving EV-based last-mile deliveries over the last few years has led to 2w EV fleet
penetration reaching an estimated 2x+ of the on-road penetration of 2w EVs in India. Our learnings through
this journey point to three constraints holding back mass EV adoption among delivery partners. With
deliveries contributing significantly to our scope 3 emissions, EV adoption is central to our Net Zero goal:
: High upfront costs vs. low full-time participation: A majority of delivery partners work part-time to
supplement existing incomes and prefer to use vehicles they already own or have access to. Investing in
a new EV is viable only for a small share of delivery partners with long-term delivery plans
. High need for credit but limited and expensive financing: Most of the delivery partners interested in
buying an EV require financing, but credit availability is limited. Those who can access financing often
face unfavorable loan terms (higher interest rates,lower loan-to-value ratios)compared to ICE vehicles
: Charging infrastructure gaps: Inadequate charging and swapping infrastructure outside major cities,
e.g., hometowns of delivery partners, creates range anxiety and undermines partners' confidence in the
long-term viability of owning an Ev
aggregators like us, EV manufacturers, infrastructure and financing players from both public and private
sectors to facilitate a just, orderly and equitable transition away from petrol-based vehicles. We continue to
consultations and industry coalitions.
We are working with experts and partners to craft new sustainable transportation goals that better reflect
our growth, diversification and on-ground realities. This exercise will lead to a revision of both of our 100%
EV-based deliveries and Net Zero goals. We will share the outcome once it concludes.

Re-evaluation of EV and Net Zero goals
Our focused efforts on driving EV-based last-mile deliveries over the last few years has led to 2w EV fleet
penetration reaching an estimated 2x+ of the on-road penetration of 2w EVs in India. Our learnings through
this journey point to three constraints holding back mass EV adoption among delivery partners. With
deliveries contributing significantly to our scope 3 emissions, EV adoption is central to our Net Zero goal:
: High upfront costs vs. low full-time participation: A majority of delivery partners work part-time to
supplement existing incomes and prefer to use vehicles they already own or have access to. Investing in
a new EV is viable only for a small share of delivery partners with long-term delivery plans
. High need for credit but limited and expensive financing: Most of the delivery partners interested in
buying an EV require financing, but credit availability is limited. Those who can access financing often
face unfavorable loan terms (higher interest rates,lower loan-to-value ratios)compared to ICE vehicles
: Charging infrastructure gaps: Inadequate charging and swapping infrastructure outside major cities,
e.g., hometowns of delivery partners, creates range anxiety and undermines partners' confidence in the
long-term viability of owning an Ev
aggregators like us, EV manufacturers, infrastructure and financing players from both public and private
sectors to facilitate a just, orderly and equitable transition away from petrol-based vehicles. We continue to
consultations and industry coalitions.
We are working with experts and partners to craft new sustainable transportation goals that better reflect
our growth, diversification and on-ground realities. This exercise will lead to a revision of both of our 100%
EV-based deliveries and Net Zero goals. We will share the outcome once it concludes.

Financial results
Consolidated revenue from operations grew 169% 
YoY to INR 54,364 crore in FY26 from INR 20,243 crore 
in FY25 primarily driven by shift to inventory model 
in quick commerce where revenue now also includes 
the full monetary value of goods sold (and not just the 
marketplace commission):
 
 Food delivery revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 10,159 
crore in FY26, primarily driven by higher order 
volumes and increase in revenue per order.
 
 Quick commerce revenue grew 626% YoY to INR 
37,779 crore in FY26 primarily driven by shift to 
inventory model where revenue now also includes 
the full monetary value of goods sold (and not 
just the marketplace commission).
 
 Going-out revenue grew 32% YoY to INR 973 crore 
in FY26 driven by growth across all categories 
including dining-out, movies and events. 
FY26 was also the first full financial year post 
acquisition of entertainment ticketing business 
in FY25.
 
 B2B supplies revenue declined 13% YoY to INR 
5,366 crore in FY26, driven by scale down of 
the non-restaurant business following the shift 
to inventory model in quick commerce. Core 
restaurant supplies business continued to grow 
YoY.
Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA improved to INR 
1,189 crore in FY26 from INR 1,079 crore in FY25. 
Improvement in Adjusted EBITDA profitability was 
primarily driven by (a) improvement in food delivery 
Adjusted EBITDA margin and (b) reduction in losses 
in our quick commerce business and B2B supplies 
business.
Consolidated EBITDA for the full fiscal year was 
positive INR 1,208 crore. Consolidated PAT declined 
to INR 366 crore in FY26 compared to INR 527 crore 
in FY25 largely due to increase in depreciation 
& amortization expense in the quick commerce 
business.
Note: To supplement our financial information presented in 
accordance with IND AS, we consider certain financial measures 
that are not prepared in accordance with IND AS, including Adjusted 
Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA. We use these financial measures in 
conjunction with IND AS measures as part of overall assessment 
of our performance to evaluate the effectiveness of our business 
strategies and to communicate with our board of directors 
concerning our business and financial performance. We believe 
these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information to 
investors about our business and financial performance, enhance 
their overall understanding of our past performance and future 
prospects, and allow for greater transparency with respect to 
metrics used by our management in their financial and operational 
decision making. We are presenting these non-GAAP financial 
measures to assist our investors and because we believe that 
these non-GAAP financial measures provide an additional tool for 
investors to use in comparing results of operations of our business 
over multiple periods. Information given also includes information 
related to material subsidiaries. Non-GAAP measures used by us 
are defined below:
a) 
 Adjusted EBITDA = Consolidated EBITDA (+) share-based 
payment expense (-) rental paid for the period pertaining to 
‘IND AS 116 leases’
b) 
 EBITDA = Profit/loss as per financials excluding (i) tax expense 
(ii) other income (iii) depreciation and amortization expense 
(iv) finance cost and (v) exceptional items

31, 2026, the Company has 16 (sixteen) direct 
subsidiaries and 4 (four) step down subsidiaries, and 
did not have any associate company or joint venture.

owned subsidiaries were incorporated and 3 (three) 
step down subsidiaries were dissolved/ liquidated as 
detailed below:

from August 8, 2025.

The Nomination and Remuneration Policy 
(“NRC Policy”) has been formulated in compliance with 
Section 178 of the Act and Regulation 19 of the SEBI 
Listing Regulations. It serves as a comprehensive 
framework governing the nomination, evaluation, 
and compensation of the Company’s directors and 
senior management personnel. The objective of 
this NRC Policy is to attract, retain, and incentivize 
talent to drive the Company’s sustainable growth and 
long-term success.
There have been no changes in the NRC Policy during 
the financial year under review. The NRC Policy is 
available at Link.
9. Number of meetings of Board
During the financial year under review, the Board 
met 8 (eight) times. The maximum interval between 
any two meetings of the Board did not exceed 120 
days. Details of the Board meetings held, including 
the attendance of the directors therein have been 
disclosed in the Corporate Governance Report 
forming part of this Annual Report.
10. Performance evaluation
The Company recognises that an effective board 
evaluation process is integral to strong corporate 
governance and supports the Board in continuously 
enhancing its effectiveness. Accordingly, the 
Company has adopted a structured framework for the 
annual evaluation of the performance of the Board, its 
committees, the chairman and individual directors, 
including independent directors.
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee 
(“NRC”), in consultation with the Board, oversees the 
evaluation framework and criteria. The evaluation, 
inter alia, considered the following aspects:
 
 Board composition, diversity and the mix of skills 
and experience;
 
 Clarity of roles, responsibilities and accountability;
 
 Quality, timeliness and adequacy of information 
provided to the Board;
 
 Effectiveness of Board deliberations, strategic 
oversight and decision-making;
 
 Leadership of the chairman and the functioning 
of the Board;
 
 Contribution and performance of individual 
directors;
 
 Effectiveness of the Board committees in 
discharging their responsibilities.
In compliance with Section 149 of the Act, Regulation 
17 of the SEBI Listing Regulations and the Company’s 
policy for evaluation of the performance of the board 
of directors, the performance evaluation of each 
independent director was carried out considering 
the aspects related to fulfillment of independence 
criteria and independence from management.
During the financial year under review, the Company 
engaged Nasdaq Corporate Solutions International 
Limited (“Nasdaq”), an independent governance 
advisory firm, to facilitate the evaluation process. The 
evaluation was conducted through a combination of 
structured questionnaires, wherein all directors were 
requested to complete comprehensive evaluation 
questionnaires tailored to capture an objective 
overview of the overall performance and one-on-one 
interviews with independent directors, providing an 
additional layer of qualitative insights and feedback.
The independent and comprehensive evaluation, 
consolidated by Nasdaq, assessed the Board’s 
overall vitality, offering deep insights into its 
leadership mindset, strategic engagement, cultural 
ethos, interpersonal dynamics, and governance 
practices.

deliberation by the Board, the findings reaffirmed 
that the Board and its committees continue to 
function effectively and provide appropriate strategic 
oversight. It also provided constructive insights 
to support the Board’s ongoing focus on strategic

the Governance, Risk & Compliance team, which 
evaluates risks based on its likelihood and impact.

supports well-informed decisions, and bolsters the 
Company’s capacity to navigate emerging risks and 
opportunities.

Risks and Concerns
In line with the Enterprise Risk Management (“ERM”) 
exercise conducted for Eternal at a consolidated 
level, below are the strategic risks that have been 
identified and may impact Eternal in the long run. 
These risks have been further mapped to the relevant 
Environmental, Social, and Governance (“ESG”) pillars 
from a sustainability standpoint, with their changing 
trends over the past fiscal year tracked closely by 
the RMC.
 Competition | Governance
Eternal faces an intensifying competitive landscape 
across both established and emerging segments, 
which can directly hinder growth, compress operating 
margins, and reduce overall platform revenue and 
profitability. Key risk factors include capital-fueled 
expansions by quick commerce rivals and the entry 
of new players. Furthermore, aggressive competitor 
tactics—such as eliminating user handling fees 
and lowering delivery fee thresholds—exert strong 
pricing pressure, triggering risk of customer 
migration or heightened monthly inactivity on our B2C 
marketplaces.
To protect market share and strengthen our 
operational moats, Eternal continues to evolve its 
business strategy from rapid expansion to sustained 
efficiency. Blinkit has strategically transitioned to an 
inventory-owned model to achieve absolute control 
over pricing, product availability, and margins, 
supplemented by Hyperpure entering the B2C market 
as a core seller for fresh and perishable products. 
Concurrently, Zomato has scaled user retention 
and expanded affordability features by introducing 
consumer-centric options like “Healthy Mode” and 
budget-conscious “Meals under 250,” while the 
District app continues to establish exclusive global 
partnerships with international agencies to secure 
premium event inventories.
Driven by execution capabilities and strategic agility, 
Eternal is dedicated to sustaining its ecosystem 
leadership through disciplined cost efficiencies and 
differentiated consumer offerings.
 Regulatory Compliances | Governance 
As a leading digital platform, Eternal operates under 
an evolving legislative and supervisory framework, 
where any failure to track, interpret, or communicate 
regulatory updates can lead to significant operational 
disruptions, heavy financial penalties, or license 
cancellations. The compliance landscape has become

Eternal is dedicated to sustaining its ecosystem 
leadership through disciplined cost efficiencies and 
differentiated consumer offerings.

windows, we actively calibrate our rate cards and

ensuring continuous fleet availability and safe 
operations through local coordination. Hyperpure is 
actively aligning its payout structures with market

has collaborated with third-party vendors to extend 
enhanced social security scheme onboarding and 
visibility to warehouse personnel. Furthermore, our 
commitment to systemic equity is reinforced through 
large-scale platforms, such as hosting the inclusive 
growth conference in New Delhi to advance collective 
partner well-being.
Recognizing that our partners form the vital 
infrastructure of our business, Eternal is dedicated 
to cultivating a fair, rewarding, and deeply sustainable 
ecosystem for all participants.
 Macro-Economics | Social & Governance
Fluctuations in localized and global economic 
conditions, alongside broader geopolitical volatility, 
can severely restrict consumer discretionary 
spending and compress corporate operating 
margins. Escalations in international conflicts pose 
severe logistics constraints, leading to dual-impact 
crises such as global energy transit bottlenecks 
that simultaneously inflate platform delivery costs 
and disrupt the fuel and LPG dependencies of our 
restaurant partners. Such structural shortages 
directly manifest as revenue bottlenecks, causing 
impact in order volumes and restricting restaurant 
supply capabilities across our core B2C and B2B 
segments.  Eternal leverages its multi-vertical 
business architecture to reduce dependency on any 
single market segment or price point, providing a 
natural cushion against macro-level discretionary 
contractions. To insulate our fleet from volatile crude 
oil metrics, Zomato and Blinkit have accelerated their 
strategic transition to EV-based logistics, optimizing 
local routes and enhancing fleet efficiency. Our 
procurement teams have strengthened supply chain 
resilience by diversifying our supplier base and 
building robust inventory reserves, while proactively 
planning for alternative energy options to protect 
our restaurant partners during macro bottlenecks. 
Through continuous macroeconomic monitoring 
and structured financial discipline, Eternal remains 
agile, maintaining its capacity to deliver long-term 
stakeholder value despite global uncertainties.
 Brand / Reputation | Governance
In an environment heavily driven by digital interactions, 
Eternal faces persistent brand exposure from adverse 
publicity, social media perception pressures, and 
ineffective customer experiences during complex 
operations. Public narratives can shift rapidly due to 
political criticism regarding gig worker welfare, public 
protests, or administrative and crowd management 
bottlenecks during major co-produced ticketing 
events. Such incidents can inflate negative social 
media mentions, trigger elevated refund requests, 
and place sudden stress on platform support 
infrastructures, presenting a challenge to long-term 
user retention and brand loyalty.  To safeguard brand 
health and maintain public trust, Eternal utilizes 
advanced analytics tools to pre-emptively monitor 
social narratives and deploy immediate corporate 
communications. We consistently validate our 
commitment to our fleet through wide-ranging 
transparency initiatives regarding partner earnings 
and have rolled out multi-city road safety campaigns 
in coordination with local authorities. For our going-
out verticals, platform features have been upgraded 
to include consumer-friendly safeguards such as a 
“Refund Guarantee Fee” for flexible cancellations 
and upfront payment capabilities to secure high-
demand inventory smoothly.  Guided by long-term 
transparency and a responsible marketing approach, 
Eternal continues to reinforce consumer trust and 
secure its brand equity across all touchpoints.
 Black Swan Disruption | Governance
Unforeseen, large-scale catastrophic events—
including severe geopolitical conflicts, regional trade 
or tariff disruptions, public health emergencies, and 
localized security incidents—pose fundamental risks to 
consumer behavior and financial stability. Given that a 
substantial concentration of group Gross Merchandise 
Value (GMV) is anchored within top-tier urban metros, 
any localized mobility restriction, trade deadlock, 
or supply shock can trigger severe operational and 
financial vulnerabilities across our consolidated 
network.  To ensure uninterrupted business continuity 
under adverse conditions, Eternal has systematically 
decentralized its operational footprint and established 
a geographically distributed supply architecture. We 
intentionally source critical inventory and materials 
from a diversified pool of independent vendors across 
separate regions, eliminating over-reliance on singular

16. Internal financial controls and 
their adequacy
As an integral component of the Company’s risk 
and governance framework, internal financial 
controls mitigate financial and operational risks to 
ensure orderly and efficient business conduct. This 
framework secures adherence to corporate policies, 
safeguards assets, prevents and detects fraud, 
maintains the accuracy of accounting records, and 
facilitates the timely preparation of reliable financial 
statements.
Commensurate with the scale of its operations, the 
Company maintains a robust internal control system 
over financial reporting. This framework ensures 
that all transactions are duly authorized, recorded, 
and reported in compliance with the applicable 
accounting standards. Key controls have been 
thoroughly documented, automated where feasible, 
and embedded directly into core business processes.
Oversight and assurance regarding control 
effectiveness are delivered to the Board through 
three structured lines of defense:
 
 Management Oversight: Maintained through 
ongoing business reviews and self-assessments.

Risk Compliance: Driven by continuous 
monitoring from the Governance, Risk, and 
Compliance function.
 
 Independent Audits: Verified through 
comprehensive design and operational testing 
by the Statutory and Secretarial Auditors.
The Company confirms that its internal financial 
controls were adequate and operating effectively 
throughout the financial year under review. This 
evaluation is further validated by the Statutory 
Auditors, whose independent testing revealed no 
material weaknesses or significant deficiencies.

continuous 
learning.

meaningful 
opportunities for growth and development, we seek

Conservation of energy 
Eternal remains deeply committed to energy 
conservation and climate action, principles that are 
firmly embedded in our operations and detailed in our 
environmental policy which is available on the website 
of the Company. Eternal continually strives to minimize 
the  overall environmental impact of its operations 
and lower its carbon footprint by prioritizing energy 
efficiency and waste management.
During the financial year under review, we 
implemented several key initiatives to advance our 
sustainability goals and drive carbon reduction:

Equipment Optimization: Use of electrical 
equipment was streamlined across the 
organisation—including air-conditioning systems, 
office lighting, and beverage dispensers—to 
minimize energy waste and maximize operational 
efficiency.

Energy-Efficient Infrastructure: Deployment of 
LED lighting and monitors was prioritised across 
our corporate offices, stores, and warehouses, 
reinforcing our commitment to sustainable 
facility management.

Culture of Conservation: To foster energy 
consciousness, we consistently distribute 
educational 
content 
across 
internal 
communication channels. These campaigns 
encourage our workforce to adopt simple, 
impactful habits, such as turning off lights in 
empty meeting rooms and unplugging fully 
charged devices.
Through these targeted efforts, Eternal is making 
substantial strides in energy conservation and carbon 
reduction, setting a strong benchmark for corporate 
sustainability and environmental responsibility.

Technology absorption 
Eternal continuously explores and deploys 
technological, product, and service innovations 
across its business portfolio. Notable recent 
advancements in financial FY26 include:

Nugget: Originally introduced in FY25, Nugget is 
an AI-native customer support platform designed 
to autonomously manage and resolve customer 
grievances. Its deployment has significantly 
accelerated query resolution times, enabled 
highly personalized support, and elevated overall 
customer satisfaction while driving substantial 
cost efficiencies. Furthermore, Nugget is offered 
as a B2B solution, allowing external businesses to 
effortlessly upgrade their own customer support 
operations.

Healthy Mode: Launched on the Zomato app in 
FY26, “Healthy Mode” empowers users to make 
highly informed dietary choices. Rather than 
focusing solely on calories, this feature assigns 
a comprehensive “Healthy Score”—ranging from 
‘Low’ to ‘Super’—to every dish based on essential 
nutritional elements such as proteins, complex 
carbohydrates, fiber, and micronutrients. Such 
information is derived from restaurants’ item 
description data and food images, which is 
analysed via our proprietary AI-model.

ANNEXURE – II
REPORT ON CSR ACTIVITIES
Brief outline on CSR policy of the Company
The Company’s CSR policy reflects its commitment to creating sustainable value for society while conducting 
its business in a responsible, ethical and environmentally conscious manner. The policy is founded on the belief 
that businesses have an important role to play in contributing towards inclusive and sustainable development 
by creating a positive impact on the communities and the environment around their areas of operation.
The Company voluntarily undertakes initiatives with the objective of supporting programmes that create 
meaningful, measurable and long-term social impact. It further enables the Company to undertake projects 
across the areas including initiatives relating to healthcare, education, livelihood enhancement, environmental 
sustainability, hunger eradication, disaster relief and other activities that address evolving societal needs. 
The Company believes that its CSR initiatives will be implemented in a transparent, accountable and efficient 
manner, with appropriate oversight and periodic review to ensure effective utilisation of resources and 
achievement of the intended outcomes.
The CSR policy also sets out the roles and responsibilities of the Board and the CSR Committee in providing 
strategic direction and oversight, including the approval, monitoring and review of CSR projects and expenditure, 
if any. During the financial year under review, there was no change in the CSR policy of the Company. The CSR 
policy is available on the Company’s website.

 Our environmental disclosures are based on the principles of operational control. These disclosures have been apportioned and 
extrapolated based on data availability, and are further discussed topic-wise as below:
Energy: Our disclosures include energy from fuel used in owned vehicles, Diesel Generator (DG) sets and purchased electricity for 
directly leased offices where we have established operational control. Energy from electricity consumed across our offices outside 
our operational control is placed within our value chain and will be taken into account in our value chain disclosures.
Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions: Our Scope 1 G>G emissions are limited to those generated by refilling of gas in owned ACs 
and fire extinguishers, fuel used in owned vehicles and directly leased DG sets. Emissions from electricity consumption in directly 
leased offices where we have established operational control are reported in Scope 2 of G>G emissions.
Water: Our boundary for water withdrawal, consumption and discharge is restricted to directly leased offices where we have 
established operational control, following the principle of operational control in accordance with Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) 
and G>G Protocol guidance.
Waste: The reporting boundary for our waste disclosures includes directly leased offices where we have established operational 
control and procured waste management services ourselves.
These environmental disclosures have been apportioned and extrapolated based on data availability.

A brief on types of customersȣ 
 
 
For the purpose of this BRSR disclosure, we have three types of customers as defined below:
 
 
1.   End-users of our platforms- End-users are customers who use our platforms to search and 
discover restaurants, read and share reviews, view and upload photos, order food, book a table, 
discover and transact across going out experiences. 
 
 
2.   Restaurant partners- We provide restaurant partners with industry-specific technological tools 
which enable them to engage and acquire customers to grow their business while also providing 
a reliable and efficient last-mile delivery service.
 
 
3.   Business partners- These include other partners onboarded on our platform to engage and 
acquire customers. We also provide business partners technological tools that enable customer 
discovery, participation in going-out experiences by offering curated offers and discounts and 
to manage certain parts of their business operations.

group entities and marketing services to a third party. Total export is 0.02% of the total revenue from 
operations of Eternal Limited for FY26. 
c. 
A brief on types of customersȣ 
 
 
For the purpose of this BRSR disclosure, we have three types of customers as defined below:
 
 
1.   End-users of our platforms- End-users are customers who use our platforms to search and 
discover restaurants, read and share reviews, view and upload photos, order food, book a table, 
discover and transact across going out experiences. 
 
 
2.   Restaurant partners- We provide restaurant partners with industry-specific technological tools 
which enable them to engage and acquire customers to grow their business while also providing 
a reliable and efficient last-mile delivery service.
 
 
3.   Business partners- These include other partners onboarded on our platform to engage and 
acquire customers. We also provide business partners technological tools that enable customer 
discovery, participation in going-out experiences by offering curated offers and discounts and 
to manage certain parts of their business operations.

of merchant outlets was made available 
as rest points for delivery partners,

and mobile charging facilities during 
their workday. The network was scaled to 
3,395 locations in FY26. We also provide 
access to custom-made and off-the-

the unpredictability of changing climate, 
including raincoats and cooling vests.
 
 In FY26, 3,000 cooling vest jackets 
were provided under a pilot to delivery 
partners to assess their effectiveness 
in reducing heat stress and to provide 
design feedback to the manufacturer.
  Carbon market instruments- We 
maintained net GHG emissions from our 
operations (classified as Scope 1 & Scope 
2) at zero by procuring verified carbon 
removal offsets equivalent to 100% of 
our Scope 1 emissions and International 
Renewable Energy Certificates (IRECs) 
for Scope 2 emissions. 
  Circular economy- Waste management 
is crucial to reducing the environmental 
impact of our value chain operations. 
Across our own offices, we have 
implemented responsible waste disposal 
and water usage initiatives. For the 
food delivery value chain we run several 
voluntary initiatives:
  Waste reduction- ‘Don’t send cutlery’ 
and the ‘Food Rescue’ initiatives are 
two key features within the Zomato 
app that help avoid the waste from 
food delivery operations. Allowing 
users to opt out of receiving cutlery 
with their order has helped avoid 
ɛ3,000 MT of cutlery waste over 4 
years. The Food Rescue feature 
enables cancelled but untampered 
food orders to be made available 
to nearby customers at discounted 
prices, helping reduce food wastage. 
Since launch in FY25, Zomato’s 
Food Rescue feature has helped 
prevent over 7.5 lakh kg of food 
waste by diverting cancelled orders 
to interested buyers (assuming each 
order weighs approximately 400g).

shelf apparel that protects partners from 
the unpredictability of changing climate, 
including raincoats and cooling vests.
 
 In FY26, 3,000 cooling vest jackets 
were provided under a pilot to delivery 
partners to assess their effectiveness 
in reducing heat stress and to provide 
design feedback to the manufacturer.
  Carbon market instruments- We 
maintained net GHG emissions from our 
operations (classified as Scope 1 & Scope 
2) at zero by procuring verified carbon 
removal offsets equivalent to 100% of 
our Scope 1 emissions and International 
Renewable Energy Certificates (IRECs) 
for Scope 2 emissions. 
  Circular economy- Waste management 
is crucial to reducing the environmental 
impact of our value chain operations. 
Across our own offices, we have 
implemented responsible waste disposal 
and water usage initiatives. For the 
food delivery value chain we run several 
voluntary initiatives:
  Waste reduction- ‘Don’t send cutlery’ 
and the ‘Food Rescue’ initiatives are 
two key features within the Zomato 
app that help avoid the waste from 
food delivery operations. Allowing 
users to opt out of receiving cutlery 
with their order has helped avoid 
ɛ3,000 MT of cutlery waste over 4 
years. The Food Rescue feature 
enables cancelled but untampered 
food orders to be made available 
to nearby customers at discounted 
prices, helping reduce food wastage. 
Since launch in FY25, Zomato’s 
Food Rescue feature has helped 
prevent over 7.5 lakh kg of food 
waste by diverting cancelled orders 
to interested buyers (assuming each 
order weighs approximately 400g).

Health, safety, 
and dignity 
for all
Risk
Ensuring a safe and 
respectful working 
environment 
is core to how 
we operate. 
Inadequate health 
& safety measures 
can lead to injuries 
or casualties 
affecting well-
being. This may 
also lead to higher 
attrition and loss 
of stakeholder 
trust. Failure to 
uphold human 
rights, including 
health & safety, 
can further expose 
the company to 
regulatory risks, 
with implications 
for business 
continuity.
  Employees and workers- Our 
occupational health & safety framework 
is supported through a comprehensive 
policy and robust workplace safety 
systems. These include mandatory 
training for employees and workers 
on health & safety, fire detection 
& fire fighting mechanisms, safety 
signage and the Safety Reporting 
System (SRS) for proactive incident 
reporting and resolution. We have 
secured ISO 45001:2018 certification 
for the Occupational Health and Safety 
Management systems in our Gurugram 
and Bengaluru leased offices. Please 
refer to Principle 3, Essential indicator 10 
for more details.

Delivery partners
  Road safety awareness and training-
All delivery partners are required to 
complete a mandatory road safety 
awareness module at the time of 
onboarding. This is supplemented by 
periodic health & safety programs 
conducted through both online and 
oũine formats. Delivery partners 
also receive educational content and 
videos on safe riding practices under 
varied weather conditions such as rain, 
heat and fog. In addition, we regularly 
organize safety camps in collaboration 
with local traffic authorities and 
have partnered with the Ministry of 
Road Transport and Highways for the 
national campaign ‘Sadak Suraksha 
Abhiyan’ promoting responsible road 
behavior among delivery partners and 
encouraging customers not to rush 
them.
  SOS service- An SOS service, 
accessible via the delivery partner 
app, is available to provide immediate 
support to all delivery partners in 
case of emergencies, including 
accidents, vehicle breakdowns, etc. 
The SOS service is set up to provide 
free ambulance to partners in 900+ 
cities, depending on the emergency. 
Ambulances are positioned to reach 
partners within 20 minutes.
  Insurance coverage- Eternal 
voluntarily provides accidental and 
medical insurance coverage, inclusive 
of disability and death benefits for all 
active delivery partners. The premium 
for this insurance is borne entirely by 
Eternal. 
Negative implication-
Inadequate health 
& safety measures 
across operations can 
increase the risk of 
work-related injuries or 
casualties, adversely 
affecting well-being. 
Failure to uphold 
human rights, including 
the right to safe 
working conditions, 
may lead to business 
disruptions, regulatory 
penalties, legal 
liabilities and cause 
reputational damage, 
resulting in negative 
financial impact.

experience home, with premium course-
wise packaging for a ‘Meal for 2’. The 
program is live in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and 
Bengaluru across 250+ restaurant brands 
and 650+ outlets.
  Zomato for Enterprise (ZFE)- ZFE is 
a platform designed for companies to 
solve food expense management. A lot 
of Zomato orders placed by corporate 
employees are business-related and need 
to be reimbursed by their employer via 
processes that are often, cumbersome 
and time-consuming. With ZFE, 
employees can simply bill their business 
orders directly to their employer, without 
having to pay, adding convenience 
for employees and transparency for 
companies. Over 350 companies have 
adopted ZFE.
  Food on Train- Long-distance Indian rail 
carries enormous passenger volumes, 
yet onboard catering has limited choices 
and inconsistent quality. Zomato’s Food 
on Train service fixes this through its 
IRCTC partnership: customers order 
on the app, enter their PNR, and pick a 
station along the route, and Zomato’s 
station walkers hand the order over right 
at the coach gate. Delivering this service 
meant building real-time train tracking 
and a dedicated layer of walker logistics 
synced to each station halt. Zomato 
delivers at 250+ stations, pan-India.

curated multi-course dining-at-
home experience from some of the 
finest restaurants, delivered directly 
to customers’ homes. Each menu 
is designed to bring the restaurant 
experience home, with premium course-
wise packaging for a ‘Meal for 2’. The 
program is live in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and 
Bengaluru across 250+ restaurant brands 
and 650+ outlets.
  Zomato for Enterprise (ZFE)- ZFE is 
a platform designed for companies to 
solve food expense management. A lot 
of Zomato orders placed by corporate 
employees are business-related and need 
to be reimbursed by their employer via 
processes that are often, cumbersome 
and time-consuming. With ZFE, 
employees can simply bill their business 
orders directly to their employer, without 
having to pay, adding convenience 
for employees and transparency for 
companies. Over 350 companies have 
adopted ZFE.
  Food on Train- Long-distance Indian rail 
carries enormous passenger volumes, 
yet onboard catering has limited choices 
and inconsistent quality. Zomato’s Food 
on Train service fixes this through its 
IRCTC partnership: customers order 
on the app, enter their PNR, and pick a 
station along the route, and Zomato’s 
station walkers hand the order over right 
at the coach gate. Delivering this service 
meant building real-time train tracking 
and a dedicated layer of walker logistics 
synced to each station halt. Zomato 
delivers at 250+ stations, pan-India.

Data privacy,

Risk 
Inadequate

measures may

Personally

Information security policy and 
framework- Eternal has formulated 
an information security policy and 
framework to protect Eternal’s data 
and information from unauthorized 
access and external threats. A dedicated 
information security team is responsible 
for monitoring the effectiveness of our 
cybersecurity policies and systems.
  ISO Certification- Eternal is committed 
to adhering to global best practices 
for data protection and continues to 
hold ISO  27001:2022 certification for 
the information security management 
systems. These practices include annual 
mandatory cybersecurity awareness for 
all employees.

Periodic assessment- Eternal 
prioritizes continuous improvement in 
cybersecurity via thorough and periodic 
review mechanisms. These include 
independent assessments such as 
audits, Vulnerability Assessment and 
Penetration Testing (VAPT) evaluations, 
third party reviews and bug bounty 
programs. These initiatives help us  stay 
vigilant and proactive in safeguarding our 
systems and data against evolving cyber 
threats.
  Investment in technologies- We invest 
in advanced cybersecurity and data 
protection technologies, reinforcing 
the control framework to mitigate 
existing and emerging risks effectively. 
We conduct regular company-wide 
awareness sessions to educate and 
empower all employees with the latest 
best practices, fostering a culture of 
vigilance and resilience across our 
organization.
  Responsible AI governance - We are 
committed to the responsible and ethical 
use of artificial intelligence across our 
business. User privacy remains a priority, 
with all data used for AI development 
and deployment maintained in secure, 
access-controlled environments 
and managed in line with ethical data 
practices. Real-time monitoring 
protocols track model performance, 
validate accuracy, and proactively 
detect and address algorithmic bias or 
data drift. AI-generated responses and 
outputs are clearly labelled so users know 
when they are interacting with artificial 
intelligence. We also conduct employee 
training and awareness initiatives to help 
them understand the ethical, legal, and 
safety considerations associated with AI.
Negative implication-
Ineffective 
cybersecurity and AI 
governance measures 
may lead to data 
breaches, service 
disruptions, and the 
loss of confidential 
or sensitive data 
including PII of key 
stakeholders. This 
may result in loss of 
stakeholder trust, 
regulatory fines, legal 
liabilities, diminished 
market reputation 
and negative financial 
implications.

Governance Leadership and Oversight
7.   Statement by director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has Ŧexibility regarding 
the placement of this disclosure) 
 
 At Eternal, we approach sustainability with the same ambition, patience and discipline we apply to building the business. We are cognizant of our responsibility in setting a 
high bar in this domain for new-age, home-grown, technology companies, like ourselves. This BRSR report showcases our progress in FY26 and reflects our commitment 
to grow in ways that are responsible, inclusive and sustainable. 
In FY26, we conducted a double materiality assessment with an independent external organization to refresh our material ESG topics. The assessment considered the 
impact of our business on people and the environment, and the implications of sustainability-related issues on long-term value creation. Our sustainability framework has, 
accordingly, been refreshed and re-organized under 4 key pillars: Climate Action and Circular Economy, Inclusive Growth, Responsible Business Leadership and Corporate 
Governance. I’ll be sharing ESG highlights from the food delivery business as per the refreshed framework.
Our work on Climate Action and Circular Economy focuses on minimizing our environmental impacts while preparing the business for changes in climate and resource 
availability. A key climate risk mitigation action is enabling EV-based deliveries. In FY26, total EV-based food deliveries stood at 132.3 million orders, 13.5% of total FY26 
food delivery orders and a 50% increase from the previous year. This achievement rode on the back of expanded EV ecosystem partnerships and the launch of our own 
EV rental fleet to match the mobility needs of delivery workers, often migrants seeking to participate in the platform on a part-time and short-term basis. In addition to 
our own efforts, the speed of this transition will require coordinated public and private stakeholder action to ensure the right EV products, adequate charging/swapping 
infrastructure and affordable financing are made available to anyone who seeks to participate and earn from deliveries. 
We are working to reduce both food and packaging waste generated by the food delivery business. Since launch in FY25, Zomato’s Food Rescue feature has helped prevent 
over 7.5 lakh kg of food waste by diverting cancelled orders to interested buyers. To reduce the environmental impact of restaurant packaging, we launched Zomato’s 
Plastic-Free Future Program in 2024 and have recognized more than 10,000 restaurants with a ‘low plastic packaging’ tag for switching out of plastic to pack their main 
menu items . Cumulative orders from restaurants using sustainable packaging crossed 100 million in FY26.
Our platform facilitates Inclusive Growth by lowering barriers to entry, enabling access to customers and creating livelihood opportunities through food orders and 
delivery. In FY26, the platform generated earnings through food delivery for 5 lakh+ restaurant partners and over 18.5 lakh unique individuals. Beyond income generation, 
we supported delivery partners through insurance, government scheme access, tax filing support and savings-related products. In FY26, over 5,500 food delivery partners 
were enrolled in at least one government scheme, unlocking access to benefits valued at over INR 120 crore.
 
 Responsible Business Leadership means maintaining our business lead by fostering innovation while protecting stakeholder trust, safety and dignity. In FY26, we 
launched Healthy Mode, to help customers make informed and healthier food choices, generating around 8.5 million orders. Our human rights assessment, conducted by 
an independent organization, found no risks, reinforcing our strength in protecting people.  As we grew, we also enabled micro-donations to Feeding India’s network to 
deliver nutritionally balanced meals to 1.4 lakh children every day. The independent initiative reached a milestone of serving 290 million meals from inception till FY26.
 
 Corporate Governance, including topics of risk oversight, ethical conduct, cyber security and data privacy, remains central to decision-making at Eternal . In FY26 we 
introduced several new measures to ensure responsible use of AI, conscious of the opportunities and risks associated with AI. Our governance and cybersecurity practices 
enabled us to ensure zero data breaches in FY26.
 
 Our efforts to date have earned us high scores in terms of ESG ratings across both Indian and global ESG rating agencies, positioning us as a leader in terms of 
sustainability. We will continue to report our progress transparently, remain disciplined in our approach, and revisit our assumptions as the business and the broader 
ecosystem evolve. More details on the ESG performance of Eternal’s non-food delivery businesses may be found on Pages 33 to 43 of our Annual Report. 
 
 - Sanjeev Bikhchandani, Non-Executive Director, Eternal Limited

responsible sourcing practices across its value chain. Initiatives taken in FY26 panned across these

 Supplier assessment: Our supplier assessment on ESG parameters is integrated into our 
supplier onboarding process. We regularly evaluate our upstream suppliers through an ESG 
questionnaire (aligned with the requirements of BRSR Core KPIs) enabling consistent monitoring

responsible business practices.

onboarding process.
 
 

Supplier partnership and recognition:
 
 
 
 
 Initiated efforts to recognise suppliers demonstrating strong ESG performance, responsible 
business practices and contributing to positive outcomes.
 
 
 
 
 Continued supplier engagement through esg-suppliers@eternal.com, to facilitate onboarding 
of sustainable suppliers and addressing supplier-related ESG queries.
 
 
 
 
 Expanded sourcing from within India by working with 1800+ MSMEs in FY25.

Company Overview
10. Health and safety management system: 
a.   Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by 
the entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage of such a system? 
Yes. At Eternal, our Health and Safety Policy includes nine pillars that outline how we effectively manage 
critical Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) aspects. Additionally, we hold the ISO 45001:2018 
certification for our OH&S Management System. The Audit Committee of Eternal Limited maintains 
oversight on health and safety related matters and reviews them on a quarterly basis.
 
 
 The Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) team helps the organization maintain high levels of safety 
standards. Our offices are equipped with essential safety systems such as fire detection, fire fighting 
mechanisms, public address systems, safety signage, etc., to ensure the safety of employees and 
workers. Additionally, there is a Safety Reporting System (SRS) that enables employees and workers 
to report OH&S incidents and hazards actively. The system ensures seamless tracking, analysis and 
resolution, thereby building a proactive safety culture and enabling continuous improvement of our 
OH&S management system. 
 
 
 Health and Safety training is mandatory for all employees of Eternal and a key pillar of our Health & 
Safety policy. In FY26, we strengthened our safety culture through a series of focused awareness 
initiatives. We marked National Road Safety month, with a mix of on-ground and digital engagement 
activities, including interactive carnivals, recognition of road safety champions under the company-
wide “Sadak Suraksha Jeevan Raksha” campaign. During this month, we also conducted engaging 
awareness initiatives across offices, emphasizing people safety and SRS reporting, while reinforcing 
the message that “safety is a habit we build together.” These efforts are further supported by 
continuous monitoring by the Workplace & Facilities team to ensure sustained adherence to safety 
standards.
b.   What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and 
non-routine basis by the entity?
 
 
 Risk identification and mitigation remain integral to our Health and Safety policy.  We adopt a proactive 
approach to identifying, assessing and mitigating hazards across both routine and non-routine 
activities. An integrated action plan is also in place to effectively respond to emergency situations.
 
 
 As part of our ISO 45001:2018-certified Occupational Health and Safety Management System, we 
follow documented procedures to systematically evaluate work-related hazards and risks across all 
operations. Employees and workers are encouraged to report hazards, near-misses and incidents 
through our Safety Reporting System (SRS), enabling structured investigation and timely closure of 
such cases.
 
 
 We continuously strengthen our approach through regular internal inspections and audits to 
proactively identify and address workplace risks. Identified risks are managed through structured 
action plans with defined timelines and measurable targets to ensure effective mitigation.
c.   Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove 
themselves from such risks. (Y/ N)
 
 
 Yes, we have established a robust process for workers to report work-related hazards and protect 
themselves from associated risks. In FY24, we introduced the Safety Reporting System (SRS), enabling 
employees and workers to report health and safety hazards, incidents, and near-misses.
 
 
 Building on this, the process is now well established across the organization. During FY26, we further 
strengthened its implementation through multiple awareness sessions, townhalls and training 
programs, ensuring it remains a reliable and accessible platform. We also ensured timely closure of 
identified risks, supported by effective Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and implementation of Corrective 
and Preventive Actions (CAPA).

environmental and social topics or if consultation is delegated, how is feedback from such

We regularly engage with our key stakeholders (end-users, restaurant partners and delivery partners) 
as outlined in our Stakeholder management policy. Each business unit in every operating location is 
required to carry out stakeholder engagement in line with the stakeholder management policy. Through 
the channels described in the policy, the functional teams in Eternal receive feedback from various groups 
of stakeholders (external and internal) on our initiatives and operations. This feedback is analyzed and 
discussed with relevant leadership teams to identify, develop and implement the environmental and 
social topics. Select actions are discussed with the CSR committee of the board based on their overall 
importance and these meetings are minuted. The CSR Committee at Eternal also undertakes responsibility 
for climate and sustainability-related matters.

Material topic: Climate action and circular economy

Zomato Plastic-Free Future Program: In response 
to customer concerns around receiving food from 
restaurants in plastic packaging, we launched the 
‘Zomato Plastic-Free Future Program’ in December 
2024. The program recognizes restaurant partners 
actively adopting sustainable alternatives to 
plastic packaging for food deliveries. More than 
350 restaurant brands, representing 10,000+ 
restaurants across 500+ cities listed on the Zomato 
app have already joined the program by submitting 
detailed evidence of their packaging, including 
photos and certificates, confirming that their 
main menu items are being packed in sustainable 
alternatives. To recognize their efforts, these 
restaurants now carry a prominent ‘Low plastic 
packaging’ tag on their menu pages, banners and a 
clear label in the order summary, making it easy for 
customers to identify these restaurants. Customers 
can also discover these restaurants faster by typing 
‘Low plastic packaging’ in the search bar or using the 
‘Low plastic packaging’ filter option. As of March 31, 
2026, we have facilitated 100 million food delivery 
orders through restaurants on the Zomato Plastic-
Free Future Program. 
Material topic: Innovation
  Healthy mode: To capture the growing demand for 
healthier meals, Eternal launched “Healthy mode” 
on the Zomato app in top 7 cities in FY26. With this 
mode, end users see a curation of  restaurants along 
with complete nutritional information, i.e. macros, 
ingredient-level description and customization 
filters. Since its launch, Healthy Mode has helped 
customers make more informed and healthier food 
choices, generating ɛ8.5 million orders in FY26.

  Social & Financial security through Government 
scheme facilitation: In FY26, in response to 
requests for support from our delivery partners, 
Eternal designed and launched a structured 
program to facilitate their better access to central 
and state government schemes. This initiative was 
designed to address key barriers faced by partners 
in accessing schemes including lack of awareness, 
time scarcity, documentation challenges and 
unclear requirements. 
 
 The program, run in collaboration with the social 
enterprise, Haqdarshak ran through a series of 
on-ground facilitation camps and digital support 
mechanisms across India. In FY26, over 5,500 
Zomato delivery partners were enrolled in at least 
one government scheme, unlocking benefits valued 
at over INR 120 crore. These benefits span critical 
areas such as healthcare, insurance and income 
support.

  Improvements in app accessibility for Persons

FY26 we launched a feature on the Zomato food 
delivery app, that enables customers to disclose

Additionally, select members of Eternal’s tech, 
product and design teams underwent the 
IAAP CPACC certification in accessibility. The

this training empowers team members to practically 
apply accessibility principles in the course of 
product development. 
3.   Provide details of instances of engagement with and actions are taken to, address the concerns 
of vulnerable/ marginalized stakeholder groups. 
Eternal has identified vulnerable/ marginalized stakeholders groups both within and outside of its value 
chain and has taken multiple actions to address their concerns.
Below are the actions taken to address concerns of vulnerable/ marginalized groups within Eternal’s value 
chain:

Zomato’s Equitable Action for Livelihood (ZEAL) program- Launched in FY23, our PwD delivery 
partner initiative has benefitted over 6,000 PwDs with a range of disabilities including locomotor 
and hearing and speech impairment. In FY26 alone 3,500+ PwD DPs, collectively delivered over 10 
million orders and covered over 40 million kms. The program benefits include waiver of onboarding 
fee, assignment of short-distance deliveries only, enhanced payouts, sensitized fleet coaches and 
support teams to better assist delivery partners as needed. In addition, restaurant partners and end-
users are notified when a PwD delivery partner is assigned to an order and requested to extend their 
support.
 
 Zomato’s Women riding centers- Facilitates two-wheeler riding training for women, basic digital 
literacy and confidence building. Through this initiative, Eternal aims to empower women by enhancing 
their mobility, enabling them to meet their personal needs with greater independence while also 
unlocking access to livelihood opportunities. Highlighted below are the benefits offered at these 
centers:
 
 

A dedicated space for women and their families to meet with company representatives, inquire 
and seek guidance on working in the gig economy. 
 
 

A safe space for women to connect, support each other, and build a sense of community.
 
 

Guidance to test and understand the available EV-bike options for interested participants.
Other initiatives to ensure women safety and support:
 
 24ɐ7 SOS emergency support: Available in 900+ cities, the emergency response system connects 
delivery partners to support like ambulance, police and an in-house response team.
 
 Address visibility at night: Between 7 PM and 5 AM, women delivery partners have the option to avoid 
locations where they may feel unsafe.

and workers. We conduct regular training and awareness sessions pertaining to various human rights

Leadership Indicators
1.   Details of a business process being modified/ introduced as a result of addressing human rights 
grievances/ complaints.
We continuously monitor, review and update our policies and processes to ensure a workplace free from 
human rights concerns. Our existing frameworks are robust, requiring no major changes to business 
processes while effectively addressing and resolving potential issues.
To reinforce our commitment, we have procedures in place, supported by grievance redressal mechanisms, 
training and awareness programs for employees. Our initiatives ensure that all stakeholders are informed of 
their rights and responsibilities, fostering a culture of respect, compliance, and ethical business conduct.
2. Details of the scope and coverage of any Human rights due-diligence conducted.
In FY26, our human rights due diligence exercise was conducted by an independent third party, and no 
significant risks were identified. Due-diligence for Eternal Limited (formerly known as Zomato Limited) 
covered all our permanent employees, other than permanent employees and third party workers (including 
migrant workers) of all genders, across all locations. 
Following aspects were covered as part of the due-diligence conducted:

Working conditions: Working hours, work-related stress, degree of safety, and comfort
 
 Labor rights: Employment contracts, freedom of association and collective bargaining, employee 
benefits, child labor, human trafficking - forced or bonded labor
 
 Rights to privacy: Protection of personal and professional data and information
 
 Health, safety and well-being: Training and awareness sessions, safety drills, insurances, assistance 
programmes and policies.
 
 Fair and equal remuneration: Compensation practices
 
 Freedom of speech: Grievance and feedback mechanisms
 
 Workplace discrimination and harassment: Discrimination (age, gender, ethnicity, sexual preference, 
color, disability, etc.) as well as mental and sexual harassment
 
 Learning and development: Skill development programs for career progression and professional growth
 
 Diversity and inclusion: Equal opportunity, diversity and inclusion
 
 In addition to an annual Human rights due diligence exercise, we also periodically review our policies and 
procedures to ensure our risk mapping of potential issues (if any) are updated and mitigated accordingly.
3.   Is the premise/ office of the entity accessible to differently abled visitors, as per the requirements 
of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016? 
Our headquarters and largest office based in Gurugram, underwent an independent external accessibility

8.   Does the entity have any project related to reducing greenhouse gas emission? If Yes, then 
provide details. 
Yes, below are the details of our projects-

Project 1: Carbon market instruments
 
 
 We have maintained 100% of our Scope 1 & Scope 2 emissions at zero through use of an equivalent 
amount of verified carbon removal offsets and International Renewable Energy Certificates (IRECs).

Project 2: Transition to EV based food deliveries 
 
 
 Our key climate risk mitigation action is to support delivery partners in transitioning to EV bikes to 
undertake food deliveries. To achieve this, we generate awareness about EVs among delivery partners, 
collaborate with EV ecosystem players to secure access to EVs on rent and advocate for better EV 
products, infrastructure and financing.
 
 

EV awareness: In FY26, delivery partners were made aware of the benefits of transitioning to 
EVs through multiple engaging videos on the YouTube channel, EV campaigns launched within the 
Zomato delivery partner app and also through notifications. We also organized the second edition 
of EV Bazaar in Bengaluru to educate the delivery partners on the benefits of EVs and to support 
their transition. Since its inception, the EV Bazaar initiative has achieved significant outreach, 
engaging over 2,000 delivery partners and more than 20 ecosystem providers across Delhi and 
Bengaluru. 
 
 

EV access: To facilitate easier access to EVs on rent, we have established partnerships with 
EV rental agencies, battery swapping companies and EV-based logistics service providers. We 
launched the Zomato EV rental fleet on World Environment Day 2025 in Delhi to enable rental 
access to quality high-speed EVs at affordable prices for delivery partners. As of March 2026, 
more than 1,500 EVs have been deployed across Delhi and Chennai under the Zomato EV rental 
fleet initiative.  
 
 

EV advocacy: We continuously advocate for better EV products, infrastructure and financing for 
delivery partners. We are a part of global coalitions on EVs including the Climate Group’s EV100 
initiative and the UNEP-supported Deliver-e Coalition. We regularly contribute to stakeholder 
consultations facilitated by central, state and city-level government on the topic of EVs.
 
 

Delivery optimization: Alongside supporting partners in adopting EVs for food delivery, we are 
continuously improving operational efficiency through delivery optimization measures that bring 
down delivery distances and time, thereby reducing energy consumption and its associated 
emissions. In FY26, delivery optimization has resulted in avoidance of 8,100 tCO2e of emissions.
 
 
 As a result of our efforts, our last-mile delivery emissions on a per km basis reduced by 11.77% in 
FY26 when compared to FY22. The total EV-based food deliveries increased by 50% compared to the 
previous year, totaling 132.3 million orders. This represented 13.5% of total food delivery orders for 
the same year.

10.  BrieŦy describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe 
the strategy adopted by your company to reduce the usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals 
in your products and processes and the practices adopted to manage such wastes.
 
 Eternal Limited (formerly known as Zomato Limited) is a technology platform services provider. Our core 
business  processes do not result in the generation of waste beyond office waste within which no toxic 
waste is generated and hazardous waste is minimal.
 
 However, we are deeply committed to effective waste management strategies to minimize environmental 
impacts of waste in our offices and in our value chain.
Office waste management
 
 Our employees sit out of leased premises or co-working spaces where waste disposal is managed by the 
owners or main lessors of the property. In offices that are directly leased by us, we have implemented 
initiatives to reduce waste and promote segregation at the source. 
 
 We promote the use of sustainable alternatives within our workplaces through provision of reusable 
cutlery and plates, implementation of a ‘Bring Your Own Bottle (BYOB)’ campaign, use of printing paper 
made from wheat straw (agri-residue). Our office coffee mugs are biodegradable and made of fallen 
pine needles, thereby reducing reliance on single-use items and virgin resources.
 
 We utilize color coded and labelled bins to ensure segregation of waste streams, supported by 
dedicated housekeeping teams. For e-waste, biomedical and hazardous waste, we appoint authorized 
vendors and obtain disposal and recycling certificates. For other waste streams such as plastic, wet 
waste and paper and cardboard, that are managed by landlords or facility operators, we obtain details 
on disposal and recycling from their appointed vendors.
 
 We conduct regular awareness campaigns and training initiatives on responsible consumption 
and disposal habits among our employees. These efforts are aimed at promoting efficient waste 
segregation at source.  
 
 We continue to invest in innovative and sustainable waste management practices. For example, 
in FY26, we onboarded Padcare as our menstrual waste management vendor across our offices. 
Padcare collects used sanitary pads and recycles them into hygienic pulp and plastic, offering a safer 
alternative to landfilling and incineration. 
 
 In line with our environmental best practices, our Gurugram and Bengaluru offices hold ISO 14001 
certification, demonstrating our commitment to effective environmental management.

Company Overview
Value chain waste management
Packaging and food waste are the two kinds of waste associated with food delivery orders sent by 
restaurants to end-consumers via the Zomato platform. Restaurants choose the kind of packaging they 
wish to use to deliver food. Restaurant practices also determine the amount of waste generated in the 
cooking process. End-consumers control the number of orders they may place, cancellation decisions and 
process of disposal of packaging and leftovers (after consuming food). We run several voluntary initiatives 
to positively influence behaviours of both stakeholders with respect to waste management. 

Reducing food and cutlery waste
 
 
 
 The Zomato app offers consumers the option of making special requests at the time of ordering, 
including a request to the restaurant not to send cutlery, thereby reducing cutlery waste. Between 
FY22 and FY26, this initiative has helped avoid over 3,000 MT of cutlery waste.  
 
 
 
 Additionally, The ‘Food Rescue’ initiative further addresses food wastage by making canceled 
orders available for nearby customers in their original untampered packaging at discounted 
prices. Since launch in FY25, Zomato’s Food Rescue feature has helped prevent over 7.5 lakh kg 
of food waste by diverting cancelled orders to interested buyers (assuming each order weighs 
approximately 400g).  
 
 Rewarding adopters and innovators of sustainable packaging 
 
 
 
 We introduced the Zomato Plastic-Free Future Program in December 2024 for restaurant partners 
actively adopting sustainable alternatives to plastic packaging for food deliveries. To recognize 
their efforts, these restaurants now carry a prominent ‘Low plastic packaging’ tag on their menu 
pages, banners and a clear label in the order summary, making it easy for customers to identify 
these restaurants. Customers can also discover these restaurants faster by typing ‘Low plastic 
packaging’ in the search bar or using the ‘Low plastic packaging’ filter option. As of March 31st
2026, over 100 million ‘Low plastic packaging’ orders had been delivered from restaurants that 
had signed up to the Plastic-Free Future Program. 
 
 
 
 To promote innovation on alternatives to plastic packaging for the food delivery use-case, we 
run an annual event on sustainable packaging bringing start-up innovators and restaurateurs to 
the same platform. In FY26, Zomato Plastic-Free Future Packathon was held in partnership with 
Startup India and Hyperpure by Zomato attracting applications from more than 125 sustainable 
packaging start-ups all over India. 

Voluntary recycling
 
 
 
 Plastic continues to play an important role in packaging for food deliveries for a few important 
reasons. Many restaurants, especially those that offer Indian and Oriental cuisine, choose plastic 
containers, trays and bottles for food deliveries on account of lack of suitable sustainable 
alternatives for liquids and ‘wet’ cuisine such as  gravies, soups and beverages. Apart from 
functional reasons, plastic is relatively affordable and more available across India. In order to 
offset the impact of plastic packaging used by restaurants on the environment, in FY23, we 
launched a voluntary plastic waste recycling initiative called the 100% plastic neutral deliveries 
initiative. Since launch, Eternal has voluntarily recycled 60,000 MT of plastic waste from FY23- 
FY26 (15,000 MT was recycled in FY26 alone) fully meeting the target of 100% plastic neutral 
deliveries as per independent estimates.

3.
Voluntary 
recycling
 
 In FY23, Zomato app launched the 100% 
Plastic Neutral Deliveries initiative. While 
the choice of packaging used for food 
deliveries rests with our restaurant partners, 
we are committed to mitigating the impact 
of this packaging on the environment 
through voluntary recycling. To estimate the 
volume of plastic used by restaurants for 
packaging, we engaged an expert third party 
to review data from orders by dish type, 
restaurant location and price of meals. This 
data was supplemented by an independent 
survey of the packaging practices of over 
600 restaurants. Zomato then engaged 
authorized waste management agencies to 
undertake recycling of plastic waste equal 
to the volume estimated by the third party 
study of restaurant packaging. 
Refer to this link for further details
 
 Since launch, Eternal has voluntarily 
recycled 60,000 MT of plastic waste from 
FY23- FY26 (15,000 MT was recycled in 
FY26 alone) fully meeting the target of 
100% plastic neutral deliveries as per 
independent estimates.
4.
Rewarding 
adopters and 
innovators of 
sustainable 
packaging 

 Plastic-Free Future Program: Restaurant 
partners choose and procure their own 
packaging for food delivery based on cuisine 
type, brand and budget. We introduced 
the Zomato Plastic-Free Future Program 
in December 2024 to recognise restaurant 
partners actively adopting alternatives to 
plastic packaging for food deliveries.
 
 To recognize their efforts, these 
restaurants now carry a prominent ‘low 
plastic packaging’ tag on their menu pages, 
banners, and a clear label in the order 
summary, making it easy for customers to 
identify these restaurants. Customers can 
also discover these restaurants faster by 
typing ‘low plastic packaging’ in the search 
bar or by using the ‘low plastic packaging’ 
filter option. 
 
 Our aim is to motivate more restaurants to 
make the switch from plastic to sustainable 
packaging alternatives while making it 
easier for environment-conscious and/or 
packaging-conscious customers to discover 
and order from these restaurants easily. A 
surge in customer awareness and usage is 
likely to drive greater adoption of sustainable 
packaging among restaurants. 
(Link: Plastic-Free Future Program) 
 
 Plastic-Free Future Program: More than 
350 restaurant brands, representing 
10,000+ restaurants across 500+ cities 
listed on the Zomato app have already 
joined the program by submitting detailed 
evidence of their packaging, including 
photos and certificates, confirming their 
main menu items are being packed in 
sustainable alternatives. As of March 
31st 2026, over 100 million ‘low plastic 
packaging’ orders had been delivered 
from restaurants that had signed up to the 
Plastic-Free Future Program.

Plastic Free Future Packathon: While 
restaurants choose their own packaging, 
alternatives to plastic packaging are limited 
in the market. To promote innovation 
on alternatives to plastic packaging for 
the food delivery use-case, we run the 
Zomato Plastic-Free Future Packathon 
in partnership with Startup India and 
Hyperpure by Zomato which serves over 
2.6 lakh+ restaurants. This annual contest 
surfaces and spotlights startups working on 
innovative sustainable packaging solutions 
for food delivery.

 Plastic Free Future Packathon: The 
second edition of the Packathon 
recognized two winners across two 
categories - ready-to-scale and prototype 
- from 128 applicants from 21 states. 47 
start-ups were led by women.
 
 Ready-to-scale startup winners Imaga 
and Go Do Good showcased bamboo 
fiber-based food delivery packaging that 
can effectively pack oily food items, and 
plant-based barrier coatings that are oil 
and grease resistant respectively. In the 
prototype category, Agrileaf Exports 
presented takeaway containers made 
of areca palm leaves with heat-sealable 
lids, and Earthworks Biomat showcased 
deliveryware made from natural fibers and 
biopolymers derived from agri-waste.
 
 Additionally, we presented the first Zomato 
Plastic-Free Packaging Awards to 24 
national and regional restaurant brands that 
have successfully shifted to sustainable 
packaging alternatives while ensuring a high-
quality customer experience.
 
 Across the two editions of the Zomato 
Packathon, many exciting innovative 
solutions have been highlighted, including 
edible cutlery, barrier coatings made of 
plant-based gums and seaweed and patented 
carry bags made of agri-waste. These 
innovations were displayed to all attendees 
through an extensive exhibition featuring 
41 enterprises working on plastic-free 
packaging solutions for food delivery. In 
FY26, Zomato Plastic-Free Future Packathon 
was held in partnership with Startup India 
and Hyperpure by Zomato attracting 
applications from more than 125 sustainable 
packaging start-ups all over India.
 
 The Zomato Plastic-Free Future Program 
(and the Zomato Packathon) is a one-of-a-
kind initiative by a food delivery platform 
globally to actively encourage the restaurant 
industry to adopt sustainable alternatives 
while working on unlocking progress for the 
Indian sustainable packaging ecosystem.
5.
Reducing food 
and cutlery 
waste

Reducing cutlery waste: The Zomato app 
offers consumers the option of making 
special requests at the time of ordering, 
including a request to the restaurant not to 
send cutlery, thereby reducing cutlery waste.

Food rescue initiative: Food wastage is a 
significant challenge, given that every month, 
around 4,00,000 perfectly good orders already 
on their way to customers are canceled on the 
Zomato app. To reduce this food wastage, we 
introduced ‘Food Rescue’, an initiative that 
makes canceled orders available for nearby 
customers in their original untampered 
packaging at unbeatable prices within minutes. 

Reducing cutlery waste: Between FY22 
and FY26, this initiative has helped avoid 
over 3,000 MT of cutlery waste in total.  

Food rescue initiative: Since launch in 
FY25, Zomato’s Food Rescue feature has 
helped prevent over 7.5 lakh kg of food 
waste by diverting cancelled orders to 
interested buyers (assuming each order 
weighs approximately 400g).

Report on Corporate Governance (CGR)
1. Company’s 
philosophy 
on 
Corporate Governance
Our corporate governance philosophy is rooted 
in integrity, transparency, accountability, and 
responsible business conduct, ensuring the protection 
of stakeholder interests and driving long-term value 
creation. This commitment to ethical and sustainable 
practices shapes our organizational decision-making 
and drives compliance with applicable laws in line with 
the charter documents of the Company in both letter 
and spirit. At the core of our governance framework 
is the strategic oversight and independent judgement 
provided by our Board, who guide the Company’s 
affairs and supervise the leadership team’s day-to-
day operations through specialized committees. 
To further foster a robust culture of accountability, 
we have implemented a comprehensive policy 
framework that includes specific codes of conduct 
for employees, senior management, and the Board, 
alongside strict guidelines for business partners and 
for prevention of insider trading.
2.Board of Directors
The Board steers the strategy, performance, and 
governance, establishing a robust operational 
framework to drive sustainable, long-term value for 
all stakeholders. The Board maintains independent 
oversight to ensure management consistently 
delivers on its commitments. The directors bring 
together a diverse mix of specialized skills and deep 
industry experience with strong leadership to execute 
its responsibilities with high efficiency.
The Board has 7 (Seven) committees comprising of 
Board members to discharge the responsibilities 
assigned to them.
Composition and inter-se relationship
During the financial year under review, the composition 
of the Board was in conformity with Regulation 17 of 
the SEBI Listing Regulations and Section 149 and 152 
of the Act. The Company operates with a one-tier 
system featuring an optimum mix of non-executive 
directors including women directors. 
The Board comprises 6 (six) directors of whom 4 (four) 
are independent directors (including 3 (three) women 
independent directors) and 2 (two) non-executive 
directors, (including 1 (one) nominee director). None 
of the directors share any inter-se relationships, each 
one of them is independent of the other, and all non-
executive directors are under the age of seventy-five 
years.
The detailed profiles of our directors and individual 
committee compositions can be accessed at Link.
Board Meetings
Our Board meets at regular intervals to deliberate 
and decide on operations, key strategic issues, and 
statutory matters. To maintain consistent momentum, 
the gap between two consecutive meetings never 
exceeds 120 days. The notice, detailed agenda 
together with relevant notes and other material 
information are generally shared with the directors 
sufficiently in advance of Board meetings, enabling 
effective deliberations and informed decision-
making.
During the financial year under review, the Board met 
8 (eight) times and all the directors of the Company 
attended at least one board meeting during such 
period. Further, the details of the Board meetings, 
AGM held during the financial year and directors’ 
attendance thereat, are provided below:
